name: Paracuellos de Jarama cemetery
story: As Nationalist troops reached Madrid in November 1936, thousands of prisoners — officers, priests, Falangists, conservatives — were taken from the Modelo, San Antón, Porlier and Ventas prisons in 'sacas' and shot beside the Arroyo de San José at Paracuellos and at Soto de Aldovea near Torrejón. It was the largest single massacre in the Republican zone. The orders for the removals came from Madrid's public-order authorities under the Junta de Defensa; the degree of responsibility of its councillor Santiago Carrillo, and the role of Soviet advisers, remain contested. The cemetery holds the mass graves and a monument erected after the war.
see: A walled cemetery on the slope with long rows of mass graves, crosses and memorial plaques listing identified victims.
plan: Managed by a private brotherhood; opening is restricted, typically mornings and on commemorative dates. Check locally before going; be respectful.

boxes.text: Death toll: modern historians mostly give 2,000–3,000 (Thomas c.2,000; Casanova c.2,700), against older claims up to 12,000. Carrillo's personal responsibility is the subject of continuing debate.
